'''Rajesh Gopakumar''' (born 1967) is an Indian [[theoretical physicist]] and the director of the [https://www.icts.res.in/ International Centre for Theoretical Sciences] (ICTS-[https://www.math.tifrbng.res.in/ TIFR]) in [[Bangalore]], India. He was previously a professor at [[Harish-Chandra Research Institute]] (HRI) in [[Prayagraj district|Prayagraj]], India.<ref name="hri-ar2011">{{cite web|url=http://www.hri.res.in/~anlweb/Annual-Report-2010-11.pdf|title=Academic Report 2010-2011|publisher=[[Harish-Chandra Research Institute]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190407045731/http://www.hri.res.in/~anlweb/Annual-Report-2010-11.pdf|archive-date=7 April 2019|url-status=live|access-date=13 June 2012}}</ref> He is known for his work on [[topological string theory]].

==Background==
Gopakumar was born in 1967 to Jaishree and G. Gopakumar in Kolkata.{{citation needed|date=March 2013}} His family hails from the southern Indian state of [[Kerala]].<ref name=toi-bhatnagar>{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/allahabad/City-scientist-chosen-for-Bhatnagar-award/articleshow/5069206.cms|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110811074439/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2009-09-29/allahabad/28066705_1_city-scientist-shanti-swarup-bhatnagar-award-bhatnagar-awardees|url-status=live|archive-date=2011-08-11|title=City scientist chosen for Bhatnagar award | date=2009-09-29|work=[[The Times of India]]|access-date=2012-06-13}}</ref> He has the distinction of securing All Indian Rank 1 in the examination for [[Indian Institute of Technology|IIT-JEE]] in 1987.<ref>[http://www.openthemagazine.com/article/nation/where-are-they-now Where are They Now? | OPEN Magazine<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

Gopakumar obtained his integrated [[M.Sc.]] degree in [[physics]] from the prestigious [[Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur|IIT Kanpur]] in 1992. He completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from [[Princeton University]] in 1997 under the supervision of [[David Gross]]. After a few years as a research associate at [[Harvard University]], he joined HRI in 2001. He was also a visiting fellow at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], [[Princeton, New Jersey]] from 2001 to 2004.<ref>[http://www.wildfire.in/wfs/wfid/yisc2009.wf/pdf/articles/yisc2009_wf_a16.pdf]{{dead link|date=December 2011}}</ref>

He is married to Rukmini Dey, a Professor of [[Mathematical physics|Mathematical Physics]] and [[Geometry]] at ICTS-TIFR.<ref>{{Cite web|title = PEOPLE {{!}} International Centre for Theoretical Sciences|url = https://www.icts.res.in/people/5/details/184/|website = www.icts.res.in|access-date = 2015-11-17}}</ref>

==Research==
Gopakumar is a [[string theorist]]. Earlier on in his career, his research was primarily focused on large N gauge theories with [[David Gross]], noncommutative gauge theories with [[Andrew Strominger]] and [[Shiraz Minwalla]], and [[topological string theory]] and gauge/geometry correspondence with [[Cumrun Vafa]] and is particularly known for proposing the [[Gopakumar–Vafa duality]] and [[Gopakumar–Vafa invariant]]s.<ref name="cornell-gopakumar-vafa">{{cite journal|last1=Gopakumar|first1=Rajesh|last2=Vafa|first2=Cumrun|author-link2=Cumrun Vafa|year=1999|title=On the Gauge Theory/Geometry Correspondence|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/25249582.pdf|url-status=live|journal=[[Advances in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics]]|volume=3|issue=1999|pages=1415–1443|doi=10.4310/ATMP.1999.v3.n5.a5|arxiv=hep-th/9811131|bibcode=1998hep.th...11131G|s2cid=13824856|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190407050214/https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/25249582.pdf|archive-date=7 April 2019}}</ref> 

Later, his work focused on attempts to derive the AdS/CFT correspondence, and on minimal model holography (with [[Matthias Gaberdiel]]). In recent years, he has made important contributions to higher spin theories and their connections with string theory (with [[Matthias Gaberdiel]]). {{Citation needed|date=December 2024}}He has also recently worked on the [[Conformal bootstrap]].

Birla Science Prize in Physics, 2004<ref name="iitk-alumniupdate">{{cite web|url=http://www.iitkalumni.org/newsupdateindetail.asp |title= News Update |publisher=IIT Kanpur Alumni Association |date=2006-03-07 |access-date=2012-06-13 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120207075359/http://www.iitkalumni.org/newsupdateindetail.asp |archive-date=7 February 2012 |df=dmy }}</ref>

* [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award]], 2009<ref name="toi-bhatnagar" />
* [[TWAS Prize]] in Physics, 2013<ref name="Prizes and Awards">{{Cite web |date=2016 |title=Prizes and Awards |url=http://twas.org/opportunities/prizes-and-awards |publisher=[[The World Academy of Sciences]]}}</ref>

He was named Fellow of the [[Global Young Academy]] of Scientists for 2010.<ref name=hri-ar2011/><ref name=gya-members>{{cite web|url=http://www.globalyoungacademy.net/members|title=Members|publisher=Global Young Academy|access-date=2012-06-13}}</ref> He is a member of the [[Indian National Science Academy]], and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>[http://www.globalyoungacademy.org/index.php/about/member/86-rajesh-gopakumar-india GYA member listing] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110116123823/http://www.globalyoungacademy.org/index.php/about/member/86-rajesh-gopakumar-india |date=16 January 2011 }}, retrieved 2011-03-23.</ref>
